Let's work on: Container With Most Water (medium)

You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines drawn such that the two endpoints of line i are (i, 0) and (i, height[i]). Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that holds the most water. Return the maximum amount of water it can store.

Constraints:
  - 2 <= len(height) <= 10^5
  - 0 <= height[i] <= 10^4

Write your solution as: def solution(height: List[int]) -> int:

Take a moment, and let me know if anything about the problem is unclear.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: The area between two lines is the shorter of the two heights times the distance between them. I want the maximum over all pairs.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Can I assume there are at least two lines in the input?

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Are we guaranteed that all the integers in the height array will be non-negative?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Let me get the brute force down first so I have something correct, then optimize. Every pair, track the max. I'm ready to start coding.

transcript.speaker: candidate
candidate
transcript.text: All passing. Now the optimization: start a pointer at each end, and always move the one pointing at the shorter line inward. The reason that's safe is that the shorter line caps the area for every pair it's part of — moving the taller pointer in can only shrink the width without ever raising the height, so you can't lose the optimum by discarding it. That gets you one pass. I'll leave the code as it is though — let's move on.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: It's O(n) time — each pointer moves inward and they meet in the middle, so every index is visited once. O(1) space, just the two pointers and the running max.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: That's everything I wanted to cover. Thanks for walking me through it.
